summary: George Thibaut was an Indologist who studied under Albrecht Weber in 1867. He served as Principal at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1879–1888) and Muir Central College (~1888–1906), and later as Registrar at the University of Calcutta (~1907–1914).
George Thomas Staunton was a sinologist who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (~1797–1799). He later served as Vice-President of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland.

George Turnour was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He served in the Ceylon Civil Service as a Member of the Supreme Council (1818) and Assistant to the Commissioner of Revenue (1820).

George Uglow Pope worked in Indology and linguistics. He led Breeks Memorial School (1859–1870) and Bishop Cotton Boys' School (1870), and later served as Lecturer in Tamil at the University of Oxford (~1884–1908).

George V. Bobrinskoy was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Lutheran Theological Seminary and Yale under Franklin Edgerton. He spent his career at the University of Chicago, serving as linguistics department chairman (1951–1967) and Emeritus Professor of Sanskrit (~1967–1985).

George Watt studied at the universities of Aberdeen and Glasgow. He held posts as Professor of Botany at Presidency University (1873–1874), worked at the University of Calcutta (~1873–1884) and the Indian Museum (~1894–1903), and lectured at the University of Edinburgh (~1907–1909).

George de Roerich worked in Tibetology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at London, Harvard, and Paris under scholars including Sylvain Lévi, he directed the Urusvati Himalayan Research Institute (~1930–1942) and headed an Indian studies section at the Institute of Oriental Studies (~1957–1960).

George van Driem is a linguist and Tibetologist who studied at the University of Virginia, Radboud University Nijmegen, and Leiden University. He held the chair of Descriptive Linguistics at Leiden (1999–2009) and served as Professor für Historische Linguistik at the University of Bern (2010–2022).

Georges B. J. Dreyfus is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics and the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, later becoming Jackson Professor of Religion at Williams College (~2003).

Georges Dumézil was a scholar of linguistics, religious studies, and history. After studying at the École Normale Supérieure under Antoine Meillet and Marcel Mauss, he taught at Istanbul, Uppsala, the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1933–1968), and the Collège de France (1949–1968).

Georges Perrot was a historian and archaeologist who studied at the École Normale Supérieure. He later served as director of the École Normale Supérieure (~1883–1904) and held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1874–1904) and the University of Paris (~1877–1908).

Georges-Jean Pinault is a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure, Sorbonne Nouvelle, and EPHE under Jean Haudry, later holding professorships at Blaise Pascal University (~1989–1996) and EPHE (from 1999).

Georgios T. Halkias is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his DPhil at the University of Oxford under Charles Ramble and later became an associate professor of Buddhist Studies at The University of Hong Kong (~2014).

Gerald Hüther studied at Leipzig University (~1971–1976). He held positions at the Max Planck Institute for Experimental Medicine (1979–1989), the University of Göttingen (~1990–2016), and Universitätsmedizin Göttingen (~1990–2016).

Gerald James Larson was an Indologist and scholar of philosophy and religious studies who studied at Columbia University. He served as a professor at UC Santa Barbara from 1972 and as Rabindranath Tagore Professor of Indian Cultures and Civilization at Indiana University (1995–2003).
Gerardus van der Leeuw was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Leiden University (~1908–1916) and held a post at the University of Groningen from 1918 to 1950.

Gereon Kopf works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Temple University and under Yasuo Yuasa, conducted research at J. F. Oberlin and Nanzan Universities, and became Associate Professor for Asian and Comparative Religions at Luther College (~1997).

Gergely Hidas is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his DPhil at Balliol College, Oxford, under Alexis Sanderson (2002–2008), served as Khyentse Fellow at Eötvös Loránd University (2007–2014), and became a postdoctoral researcher at the British Museum (2014).

Gerhard Oberhammer was an Indologist and scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Innsbruck, studied under Erich Frauwallner and V. Raghavan, and served as Professor at the University of Vienna (1964–1997).

Gerhard Wolf is a historian and archaeologist who studied at Heidelberg University (~1975–1989). He held positions at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1995–1998), Trier University (~1998–2003), and the Max Planck Society (~2003).
